Technical concerns: unbounded Gaussian encoder output contradicts compactness assumption in minorization condition; L2 convergence claim needs explicit justification for continuous latent spaces
Contradicts stated motivation: method still achieves best results with task-specific augmentations despite motivation to move beyond them
Encoder parameters fixed during inference due to computational cost, limiting adaptation to out-of-distribution instances; no ablation on updating encoder
Modest improvements over COMPASS in some settings (TSP n=100: 0.002% vs 0.014% gap); marginal gains given added algorithmic complexity

strengths: Rigorous convergence analysis for time-inhomogeneous MCMC with stochastic approximation (Theorems 5.1-5.2), extending beyond standard convexity assumptions
Excellent empirical results on TSP, achieving near-optimal solutions (0.002% gap with augmentation at n=100)
Clear problem motivation articulating limitations of prior work (CVAE-Opt, COMPASS, augmentation dependency)
Comprehensive ablation studies (Tables 3, Figure 3) effectively demonstrating value of interacting MCMC and SA components
Good reproducibility with released code, detailed hyperparameters, and comprehensive appendices
Well-written with clear problem formulation and generally good exposition
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: LGS-Net is a straightforward encoder-decoder VAE; instance-conditioning is standard in conditional generative models. The distinction from CVAE-Opt (using p_ϕ(z|x) vs q_ϕ(z|x,y)) is a minor architectural choice

Theoretical contributions are incremental: Theorem 5.1 uses standard minorization/drift techniques for Metropolis-Hastings; Theorem 5.2 has Assumption 4 (convergence of θ_m) which appears somewhat circular—it assumes what SA should guarantee. Convergence bounds on distribution don't translate to CO solution quality guarantees

Experimental concerns: (1) Only compares against two latent-space baselines (CVAE-Opt 2021, COMPASS 2023); (2) Marginal CVRP improvements without augmentation (LGS -0.102% vs EAS -0.205% vs COMPASS -0.057% at n=100); (3) No error bars despite 1000-instance averages; (4) EAS sometimes outperforms on CVRP-150 despite higher per-iteration cost, questioning fairness of time comparison

Ad-hoc methodological choices: SA update schedule [1,1,5,15,25,100,150] appears manually tuned without principled justification. Theoretical analysis assumes continuous parameter convergence but implementation uses periodic updates. Encoder ϕ frozen during inference without ablation justification
Severe scope limitation: Only evaluated on TSP/CVRP routing problems. No evidence of applicability to other CO domains (matching, scheduling, subgraph, etc.), limiting generalizability claims
High hyperparameter complexity with manual tuning requirements: d_z, σ², λ, β, τ schedule, and SA schedule. Raises concerns about application to new problem domains without significant re-engineering

Weak assumption verification: Assumption 4 (||θ_m - θ_∞||²_L2 = O(a_m)) is stated but never empirically verified. No verification that decoder probabilities are bounded away from zero or gradient bounds (Assumption 3) hold in practice
Proposal distribution (using differences between random particles) is unconventional with limited justification. No ablation on design choices like fixed-interval vs learned proposal adaptation

Claims of novelty overstate contributions: 'Instance-conditioned latent space' presented as major contribution but standard in conditional VAE literature. MCMC+SA combination, while reasonable, is well-known

strengths: Novel theoretical contributions: Rigorous convergence analysis for time-inhomogeneous MCMC without requiring strict convexity/coercivity, with new general results in Appendix D that have independent value
Well-motivated architectural design: Instance-conditioned latent space addresses real limitations of COMPASS and CVAE-Opt by requiring neither labeled data nor pre-trained policy
Strong empirical results: Near-optimal TSP solutions, state-of-the-art among RL-based CO methods, consistent improvement over COMPASS, good out-of-distribution generalization to n=125,150
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Systematic comparisons with multiple baselines, ablation studies clearly demonstrating component contributions, evaluation both with/without augmentation trick
Clear presentation: Well-structured paper with detailed supplementary material, good visualizations of latent space and convergence behavior, comprehensive notation appendix
weaknesses: Limited architectural novelty: Latent model follows straightforward encoder-decoder design using Kool et al. (2019) structure; instance conditioning is natural but not innovative; novelty claims somewhat overstated

Theory-practice gap: Convergence guarantees apply only to inference not training; Theorem 5.2 allows convergence to arbitrary critical points rather than optimal solutions, limiting practical interpretation

Method complexity and hyperparameter sensitivity: Inference involves numerous ad-hoc parameters (update schedule manually chosen without extensive tuning, K-dependent performance, problem-specific σ²/γ values); raises reproducibility concerns

Limited experimental scope: Evaluation restricted to TSP/CVRP only despite mentioning Knapsack/Job Scheduling in introduction; training only at n=100, testing up to n=150; critical limitation: EAS outperforms LGS-Net on CVRP n=150, suggesting scalability issues

Experimental reporting gaps: No confidence intervals or significance tests for main results; improvements often marginal (0.001-0.08% gaps); no wall-clock time comparisons despite computational complexity claims; missing ablations on latent dimension and other key hyperparameters

strengths: Solid theoretical contributions with new convergence analysis for time-inhomogeneous MCMC with Stochastic Approximation, extending beyond existing results
Well-motivated design addressing limitations of prior work: instance-conditioned encoder (vs COMPASS) and RL training without labels (vs CVAE-Opt)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with extensive baselines, ablations on key design choices, and tests on generalization
State-of-the-art and consistent empirical results across TSP and CVRP benchmarks
Reproducible research with publicly available code and detailed hyperparameters
Clear presentation with good motivation and comprehensive appendices demonstrating ablations on instance-conditioning, stochasticity, and prior choices
weaknesses: Significant scalability limitations: main experiments on n≤150 with only one n=200 experiment; solutions for larger instances remain vague, severely limiting practical applicability
Tenuous connection between theory and practice: convergence theorems prove stationarity in total variation distance but don't characterize convergence to good solutions or solution quality

Multiple carefully-tuned hyperparameters (K, update schedule [1,1,5,15,25,100,150], σ², γ, λ, β, R) with limited sensitivity analysis; update schedule appears manually tuned without principled justification

Modest empirical improvements in several cases (CVRP n=100: ~0.24% improvement over COMPASS; CVRP n=150 with augmentation: EAS actually outperforms); improvements often <0.1% without reported confidence intervals
Limited scope of demonstrated extensions: claims generality but only validates on knapsack; CVRP-TW and JSSP sketched but not experimentally tested
Missing analysis of failure modes and limited discussion of when/why method underperforms; e.g., why does EAS outperform on CVRP n=150 with augmentation?

strengths: Rigorous convergence analysis for time-inhomogeneous MCMC with theoretical guarantees (Theorems 5.2-5.3)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with extensive ablations (instance-conditioning, stochasticity, inference variants) and detailed hyperparameter studies
Well-motivated instance-conditioned latent space that naturally extends beyond COMPASS
Strong reproducibility practices with detailed implementation details, extensive appendices, and promised code release
Careful experimental methodology comparing against numerous baselines (POMO, EAS, COMPASS, ELG, CNF) with both augmented and non-augmented settings
weaknesses: Marginal practical improvements over COMPASS (0.01-0.4 percentage points), often within noise margins for this problem class and comparable to baseline variations
Critical theory-practice gap: Assumption 4 (parameter convergence rate) is never empirically verified; convergence guarantee is therefore conditional. No finite-sample rates provided
Excessive method complexity with many hyperparameters (latent dimension, radius, update schedule, learning rates, temperatures) yielding modest improvements that don't justify engineering burden
Limited practical applicability: experiments restricted to n≤200; inference budget of 40M units (~2 seconds/instance) is generous; acknowledged inability to handle global constraints
Incremental novelty: instance-conditioning is natural extension of standard VAE conditioning; MCMC and SA are direct applications of existing techniques; main contribution is careful engineering

strengths: Novel combination of instance-conditioned latent space with MCMC-based inference, directly addressing limitations of prior work (COMPASS lacks instance conditioning, CVAE-Opt requires labeled data)

Strong theoretical contributions: Theorem 5.3 on time-inhomogeneous MCMC with stochastic approximation extends beyond existing results by avoiding strict convexity/coercivity assumptions unsuitable for discrete problems
Comprehensive experimental validation with state-of-the-art results on TSP/CVRP benchmarks, thorough ablations isolating contributions, and reproducible code
Principled design choices: cost-weighted training loss well-motivated via importance sampling; computational efficiency considerations (updating only final layer) are justified and ablated
Clear error decomposition in Theorem 5.3 (mixing, tracking, optimization components) provides actionable insights into convergence behavior
Systematic demonstration of extensibility to CVRP-TW, JSSP, and knapsack problems shows framework generality
weaknesses: Significant scalability limitation: main experiments n≤150; CVRP200 results (Table 11) show advantage diminishes; fundamental issue is linear growth of decoding horizon T with instance size, which remains unresolved

Empirical improvements are often modest: ~0.2-0.3% over COMPASS/EAS on TSP/CVRP; on out-of-distribution instances (n=125,150), improvements are 0.01-0.34%, raising questions about practical justification for added complexity

Theoretical assumptions require careful verification: Assumption 4 (θ_m convergence) needs smoothness of test objective; non-asymptotic rate is slow (O(m^{-1/2}log m)); limited guidance on verification for new problems

Hyperparameter complexity underexplored: many parameters (K, R, d_z, λ, τ schedule, SA update schedule) with limited principled guidance for setting them; update schedule [1,1,5,15,25,100,150] appears manually tuned
Out-of-distribution generalization advantage over COMPASS is modest; Table 7 validates instance-conditioning but doesn't demonstrate dramatic benefits, somewhat overstating the claimed advantage

Presentation: critical results relegated to appendices (Tables 4-5, extensive ablations); main paper heavy on theory with limited practical guidance; adding ~20 pages of appendices reduces accessibility
